layout.title: How a dam works

shows.does: a stepped dirt bank stands across the valley in section
rain fills the lake, it pours over the top and the dirt bank slides away downstream; a leaf floats on the lake
a tall concrete wall rises across the valley
arrows push on the wall from the deep water and a crack splits its base
the wall becomes a stepped wedge, thick at the bottom, and the crack is gone
a glowing outline traces the wedge
the lake rises in the storm and water pours over the top of the wedge, carrying the leaf toward the dam
a concrete spillway carries the extra water down the dam face, the leaf rides down it
the falling water tears a hole in the riverbed below the dam
a concrete apron fills the hole at the foot of the spillway
the river below the dam drains away and the town beyond is left dry
a gate at the dam's base slides up and a steady stream runs through to refill the river
the lake sits full behind the wedge, the steady stream runs out below and the leaf drifts on downstream
the dam holds the full lake

layout.why: The valley in section: the lake on the left, the dam in the middle, the river and a town downstream on the right, so the water's own path (lake, dam, spillway, riverbed, town) orders the story. A leaf rides the water from the lake over the spillway and down the river; each problem is physical (the bank washing away, a crack, water pouring over the top, a hole torn in the riverbed, the river running dry) and the end shows the full lake behind the wedge with a calm river below.

sentences.text: If you pile dirt across a valley, you have a dam.
But the lake spills over and washes the dirt away.
So you build a concrete wall instead.
But deep water pushes so hard the wall cracks.
So you make it a wedge, thick at the bottom.
But a storm pours water over the wedge.
So a spillway carries the extra water down.
But the spillway's rushing water digs out the riverbed.
So concrete steps slow the water at the bottom.
But below the steps, the riverbed sits empty.
So gates let a steady flow through.
Let the lake fill the valley, and the river runs calm.
Congratulations, you have built a dam.

recurring.what: a leaf floating from the lake over the spillway and down the river
